text:
Zach Werenski won the Norris last season, and the Blue Jackets' bumpy start hasn't dimmed him. He plays nearly 28 minutes a night, has 21 points in 22 games and a five-game point streak, and set another franchise record in Toronto. Evolving-Hockey had him fourth among all defensemen in wins above replacement last year.

The hot run is earned on his own shots: 11 points in ten games with more chances than usual (2.4 expected goals against his normal 2.0), and All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts him at the 99th percentile among defensemen for chances from the home plate. Not many blueliners live there. What won't last is the team's finishing around him: Columbus has scored 11.5 more goals than expected with him on the ice, while the five-on-five chances run about even (49%). He also blocks shots like a stay-at-home type, 48 already. His ice time is down two minutes a night lately, worth watching. Our range projects 69 to 95 points.
